study: Retrospective checkpoint-bound temperature scaling and opt-in abstention

fit.objective: mean negative log-likelihood in natural logarithms

policy.selection: Fixed in advance for illustration; not tuned on validation or test outcomes
policy.accept_rule: calibrated probability of unchanged predicted class >= 0.90

secondary: multiclass Brier: mean sum of squared class probability errors
accepted/deferred counts, coverage, accepted errors and denominator
evaluation.aggregate: Arithmetic mean across three seeds; any spread is sample SD, not a confidence interval

limitations: Validation was used for checkpoint selection in all three original fine-tunes.
Five exact raw inputs overlap training and validation; none overlap validation and test.
Recorded identifiers and exact raw-input equality do not prove capture independence.
Released pretraining checkpoint exposure remains unknown.
The test data has been examined previously; this is retrospective, not a fresh independent holdout.
A positive scalar temperature preserves the maximum-logit class; no accuracy improvement is claimed.
Calibration is data-dependent; 0.90 is not a guaranteed probability of correctness or a safe blocking threshold.
